text:
ana: thinking about reroutes when the gateway forwards to a new edge - we lose some call context and partial stream state. proposal: attach a small deterministic snapshot to the reroute token so downstream can resume without re-computing KV cache.

sam: curious what you mean by 'deterministic snapshot' — full KV dump will be huge.

ana: not a full dump, more like a compact checkpoint: last-token-id, prefix-hash, active-stream-offsets, and a pointer to cached prompt fragments. tiny, verifiable.

jin: two concerns: 1) privacy (we might expose prompt fragments across tenants) 2) validation cost when resuming.

ana: for privacy: we can encrypt the checkpoint with the customer's KMS key (Private/Dedicated) or sign it with per-tenant HMAC so only authorized proxies accept it.

marta: validation: how do we ensure the resumed execution yields the same logits/kv positions? ML models are non-deterministic at times due to fp kernels/quantization.

ana: good point. checkpoint is only for routing/kv lookup to avoid re-tokenizing and re-attaching cached prefix. final determinism for generation not required, it's about restoring cache indexes and offsets to avoid reprocessing long prefixes. we still rely on model-variant compatibility checks.

sam: operational tradeoffs: bigger checkpoint -> fewer re-computes but more network/serialization cost. smaller checkpoint -> cheaper handoff but could force re-encoding the prefix at the new node. suggest adaptive size based on request length and SLO.

jin: suggestion: a two-tier handoff protocol: 1) lightweight token with essential pointers and checksum 2) optional async fetch of detailed fragments from origin cache (over internal trusted channel) if the new node decides it's worth it.

ana: exactly. fallback path: if checksum mismatch or model variant incompatible, new node rejects resume and triggers graceful fallback to re-decode prefix with a short hedging delay.

marta: what about backpressure and ordering semantics across the reroute? client expects monotonic stream IDs and no duplication. We need to ensure in-flight tokens already acked don't get replayed.

sam: protocol idea: assign a monotonic stream-epoch id on initial connect. any reroute increments epoch and includes 'replay-window' which the client can use to ignore duplicates. gateway maintains a small blackhole window for late packets for N seconds to absorb duplicates.

jin: addendum: include an idempotency vector of recently-sent event IDs in the checkpoint so downstream can dedupe easily without global coordination. tiny bloom filter could work.

marta: bloom filters are probabilistic; we need near-zero chance of accidental drop. keep it as optional optimization. default: explicit recent-ID list up to M=50 events.

ana: implementer notes: config knobs per-route: resume.enabled (bool), resume.checkpoint_size (tiny/medium/full), resume.async_fetch (bool), resume.replay_window_sec (int). Also route.policy: prefer-local-cache vs. fresh-start.

sam: can we mock up a minimal protocol snippet for the proxy?

ana: posting quick snippet:

```
POST /proxy/reroute
Headers:
  X-Stream-Epoch: 42
  X-Resume-Token: base64(...) // encrypted checkpoint
Body: empty

Response 200
Headers:
  X-Resume-Accepted: true
  X-Replay-Window: 3
```

jin: ops-bot: any infra concerns?

ops-bot: deploy-bot: noted. we need an SLO runbook: if resume.accepted && model-variant-mismatch -> autopinned fallback to compatible variant within 200ms or return controlled abort to client. Also metrics: resume.accept_rate, resume_mismatch_rate, average_resume_latency.

marta: action items: ana to write a short RFC with state format + encryption options; jin to prototype async fetch; sam to add route config knobs and metrics; ops to propose runbook thresholds.

ana: will draft RFC by EOD Wednesday. thanks all :thumbsup:
